'''''Amphiroa''''' is a genus of thalloid [[red algae]] under the family [[Corallinaceae]].

== Taxonomy and nomenclature ==
Amphiroa was first described by [[Jean Vincent Félix Lamouroux]] in 1812 with the type species for the genus being ''Amphiroa tribulus''<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last=Lamouroux |first=J.V.F. |date=1812 |title=Extrait d'un mémoire sur la classification des Polypiers coralligènes non entièrement pierreux. |journal=Nouveaux Bulletin des Sciences, par la Société Philomathique de Paris |volume=3 |pages=181–188}}</ref>''.'' This genus was named after Amphiro, a sea nymph in the epic poem of Theogony by the Greek poet Hesiod.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last1=Guiry |first1=M.D. |last2=Guiry |first2=G.M. |date=2023 |title=Amphiroa J.V.Lamouroux, 1812 |url=https://www.algaebase.org/search/genus/detail/?genus_id=y9facef3001b8d7e1 |access-date=19 January 2023 |website=AlgaeBase}}</ref> There are currently 72 accepted species names for this genus.<ref name=":1" />

== Morphology ==
''Amphiroa'' is composed of an erect thallus that is attached to the substrate with an insconspicous crustose base, and possess mature branches differentiated into alternating areas calcified intergenicula and uncalcified genicula that is composed of more than cell layer and does not exhibit any dimerous flange-like branches.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Woelkerling |first1=W.M.J. |last2=Sartoni |first2=G. |last3=Boddi |first3=S. |date=2002 |title=Paulsilvella huveorum gen. & sp. nov. (Corallinaceae, Rhodophyta) from the Holocene of Somalia and Kenya, with a reassessment of Lithothrix antiqua from the Late Pleistocene of Mauritius |url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.2216/i0031-8884-41-4-358.1 |journal=Phycologia |language=en |volume=41 |issue=4 |pages=358–373 |doi=10.2216/i0031-8884-41-4-358.1 |s2cid=86442902 |issn=0031-8884|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite journal |last1=Harvey |first1=Adele S. |last2=Woelkerling |first2=William J. |last3=Millar |first3=Alan J.K. |date=2009-07-01 |title=The genus Amphiroa (Lithophylloideae, Corallinaceae, Rhodophyta) from the temperate coasts of the Australian continent, including the newly described A. klochkovana |journal=Phycologia |volume=48 |issue=4 |pages=258–290 |doi=10.2216/08-84.1 |s2cid=84444359 |issn=0031-8884}}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite journal |last1=Norris |first1=J.N. |last2=Johansen |first2=W.H. |date=1981 |title=Articulated coralline algae of the Gulf of California, Mexico. I. Amphiroa Lamouroux. |journal=Smithsonian Contributions to the Marine Sciences |volume=9 |page=32|doi=10.5479/si.1943667X.9.1 }}</ref> Specimens can reach around 30 cm in size. The thalli take a crustose form; [[dichotomous branches]] are formed. The organisms possess secondary [[pit connection]]s. ''Amphiroa'' reproduces by means of [[conceptacle]]s; it produces tetraspores. Its pore canals are lined with parallel filaments; the morphology of the pore canal is a key trait used to delineate species within the genus.<ref name="Harvey2009">{{Cite journal |last1=Harvey |first1=A. S. |last2=Woelkerling |first2=W. J. |last3=Millar |first3=A. J. K. |year=2009 |title=The genus ''Amphiroa'' (Lithophylloideae, Corallinaceae, Rhodophyta) from the temperate coasts of the Australian continent, including the newly described ''A. klochkovana'' |journal=Phycologia |volume=48 |issue=4 |page=258 |doi=10.2216/08-84.1|s2cid=84444359 }}</ref>

== Distribution ==
''Amphiroa'' is a cosmopolitan genus inhabiting the tropics up to the temperate regions.<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":3" />

== Ecology ==
This genus is found from the intertidal down to the subtidal areas of the reef.<ref name=":3" />

== Life history ==
''Amphiroa'' exhibit a triphasic life cycle, however, their tetrasporangia, spermatangia, and carposporangia are borne out of a specialized organ called a conceptacle. This triphasic cycle involves the production of tetraspores (N) from the tetrasporophyte (2N) and the subsequent development of the tetraspores into either the male or female gametophyte (N); the resulting spermatium produced by the male gametophyte is later on trapped by the trichogyne of the female gametophyte leading to their eventual fusion and development of the carposporophyte (2N); the cycle is complete when the carpospores (2N) are released and develops into the next set of tetrasporophytes.<ref name=":3" /><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Johansen |first=H.W. |title=Reproduction of the Articulated Coralline Amphiroa Ephedraea |date=1968 |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/j.1529-8817.1968.tb04702.x |journal=Journal of Phycology |language=en |volume=4 |issue=4 |pages=319–328 |doi=10.1111/j.1529-8817.1968.tb04702.x |pmid=27068206 |s2cid=24515929 |issn=|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

== Exploitation, harvesting, and cultivation ==
''Amphiroa'' species are unpalatable due to its thallus being highly calcified, and thus there is no immediate cultivation and use for the seaweed.

== Chemical composition and natural products chemistry ==
''Amphiroa'' contains several bioactive compounds similar to other seaweeds, for example, the ellagic acid, gallic acid, and phenolic compounds within ''A. anceps'' has shown to be a potential anti-fungal agent,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=El-Bilawy |first1=E.H. |last2=Al-Mansori |first2=A.A. |last3=Soliman |first3=S.A. |last4=Alotibi |first4=F.O. |last5=Al-Askar |first5=A.A. |last6=Arishi |first6=A.A. |last7=Sabry |first7=A.E.N. |last8=Elsharkawy |first8=M.M. |last9=Heflish |first9=A.A. |last10=Behiry |first10=S.I. |last11=Abdelkhalek |first11=A. |date=2022 |title=Antifungal, Antiviral, and HPLC Analysis of Phenolic and Flavonoid Compounds of Amphiroa anceps Extract |journal=Sustainability |language=en |volume=14 |issue=19 |article-number=12253 |doi=10.3390/su141912253 |issn=2071-1050|doi-access=free }}</ref> moreover, the addition of ''A. fragilissima'' polysaccharides have shown to improve the gut of farmed shrimp.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Muttharasi |first1=C. |last2=Gayathri |first2=V. |last3=Muralisankar |first3=T. |last4=Mohan |first4=K. |last5=Uthayakumar |first5=V. |last6=Radhakrishnan |first6=S. |last7=Kumar |first7=P. |last8=Palanisamy |first8=M. |date=2021 |title=Growth performance, digestive enzymes and antioxidants activities in the shrimp Litopenaeus vannamei fed with Amphiroa fragilissima crude polysaccharides encapsulated Artemia nauplii |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S0044848621009261 |journal=Aquaculture |language=en |volume=545 |article-number=737263 |doi=10.1016/j.aquaculture.2021.737263|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

== Utilization and management ==
This genus is currently not being utilized and managed on a commercial scale due to a lack of culture technology.
